business_scope.primary_industry_name: Multi-Parameter Bedside Telemetry Monitor Assembly and Calibration

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Code de commerce, Book II, Articles L. 210-1 to L. 210-10 and L. 223-1 to L. 223-43 (Société à Responsabilité Limitée); Code civil provisions on contributions and corporate formalities.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Greffe du tribunal de commerce (Registre du commerce et des sociétés, RCS) through the Guichet des formalités des entreprises operated by INPI.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Formulaire M0 – Demande d'immatriculation au RCS d'une société commerciale
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum capital for SARL; capital must be fixed in the articles and fully subscribed. Cash contributions must be paid in at least 20% on incorporation, with the balance due within 5 years; in-kind contributions must be fully paid at formation. Cash contributions must be deposited into a bank account or the Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations if the articles are not notarized.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the subscribers hereby accept the terms of the articles of association of the SARL, and confirm their respective share subscriptions and initial capital contributions as set forth therein. FURTHER RESOLVED, that the registered office is established at [address], as stated in Article 4 of the articles. FURTHER RESOLVED, that [Name] is appointed as Manager for an indefinite term, with the full powers to act on behalf of the company in all circumstances, under ordinary and extraordinary management authority, and that any required regulatory filings shall be executed. All actions taken pursuant to these resolutions are ratified.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting of Articles of Association and Capital Subscription
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary or legal counsel; applicable bank or Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations for capital deposit
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare and validate the statuts, including corporate name, registered office, share capital, subscriber/allocation of quota, management clauses, and litigation rights. Open a blocked bank account for cash contributions if the articles are not notarial, or execute notarial statuts recording contribution payments. Ensure in-kind contributions are appraised and fully delivered.
required_dossiers: Proof of registered office address (lease or ownership title)
Bank deposit certificate or notary attestation of capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Amend the articles by a private deed and re-submit; correct capital payment evidence and re-deposit if the bank certificate contains errors.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic Filing of M0 Application on Guichet Unique
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INPI Guichet des formalités des entreprises (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Access the online portal, complete the M0 incorporation questionnaire, upload the required dossier, make payment of the electronic filing fee, and submit. The application is then routed to the relevant Greffe for RCS registration.
required_dossiers: Bank certificate of capital deposit or notarial attestation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried or returned incomplete, correct inconsistencies within 15 days in the Guichet unique and resubmit; obtain a lawyer's attestation if the registry challenges the statut provisions.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration in the RCS and Issuance of Kbis Extract
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Greffe du tribunal de commerce (territorially competent)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The Greffe processes the transmitted dossier, verifies legal compliance, and enters the SARL in the Registre du commerce et des sociétés. The company receives an RCS number and an official Kbis extract, which constitutes the commercial identity certificate.
required_dossiers: Transmitted M0 dossier from Guichet unique
Proof of payment of registry fees
Any request for priority or urgent registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Appeal or cure by requesting the Greffe to correct clerical errors; provide omitted supporting documents; if refusal is sustained, apply to the judge of the commercial court (juge commis à la surveillance du RCS).

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication of Incorporation Notice in a Legal Gazette
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Journal d'annonces légales (JAL) authorized in the department of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the incorporation notice to the chosen legal gazette. The notice must contain the company name, form, capital, registered office, manager(s), RCS number, and RCS city. The JAL issues an attestation of publication, which is part of the final registry file.
required_dossiers: Extract of statuts regarding corporate identity
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If publication is delayed or notice is defective, reissue a corrected publication and provide the proof to the registry; use an expedited JAL if the deadline is urgent.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Registration Administrative, Tax, and Social Formalities
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) and URSSAF / social security authorities
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Use the Kbis extract to complete the tax registration (form 1200/Form D0) and employer registration. Obtain French SIRET, SIREN, TVA intra-communautaire number, and employer codes. Also file the publication attestation with the RCS dossier if not already transmitted.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Notify the Greffe of any missing publication attestation; contact DGFiP to activate tax and VAT registration; rectify payroll declarations through URSSAF after initial registration.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Agence nationale de sécurité du médicament et des produits de santé (ANSM) and, for industrial site compliance, the Direction Régionale de l'Environnement, de l'Aménagement et du Logement (DREAL)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Enregistrement ANSM en qualité de fabricant de dispositifs médicaux (Medical Device Manufacturer Registration, including EU CE marking conformity for bedside patient monitors under EU MDR)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de la Transition Écologique / Direction Régionale de l'Environnement, de l'Aménagement et du Logement (DREAL) and Inspection des Installations Classées
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Enregistrement (Category B ICPE) for low-to-medium impact assembly and calibration; full Environmental Impact Assessment required if hazardous waste or VOC emission thresholds exceed French nomenclature limits
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with EU Industrial Emissions Directive 2010/75/EU and French arrêtés ministériels; wastewater discharge limits (e.g., pH 6.5-8.5, COD below 125 mg/L, TSS below 35 mg/L), VOCs below 150 mg C/m3 in gaseous emissions, and hazardous waste disposal under the Code de l'environnement.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification from the commission de sécurité, structural load inspection of the premises, and workplace health and safety clearance by the Inspection du travail before production start.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) – French public finance authority; online portal: impots.gouv.fr; business entity registration through the Guichet Unique at formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a French SARL, the statutory representative files the incorporation dossier with the Guichet Unique (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr). The CFE/Guichet Unique transmits the data to INSEE and DGFiP; the entity receives a SIREN (9-digit) and, after starting taxable activity, a French intra-Community VAT number (FR + 11 characters). Non-French entities with no establishment in France that owe French VAT must apply directly to the competent SIE (Service des Impôts des Entreprises) using form 1547-SD, and non-EU applicants are generally required to appoint a tax representative in France. EU-established suppliers may instead use OSS/IOSS where their distance sales stay below prescribed thresholds. A foreign parent owning shares in the SARL does not trigger a separate French tax ID.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box election in France. A small/medium 'family' SARL meeting the criteria of CGI Art. 239 bis AA may elect to be taxed as a partnership under the personal income tax regime (IR) instead of the default corporation tax (IS). A French-headquartered SARL group may elect 100% tax consolidation ('intégration fiscale') under CGI Art. 223 A et seq. Other options include the 'régime mère-fille' participation exemption and ATAD hybrid-mismatch neutralizing adjustments (CGI Art. 212 bis).

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée – TVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general registration threshold for foreign or French taxable persons making taxable supplies in France. A French-established SME may use the franchise en base exemption only if annual turnover does not exceed EUR 85,000 for sales of goods (EUR 34,400 for services; 2024/2025 limits), but a SARL engaged in manufacturing and selling patient monitors normally must obtain a VAT number from inception. Non-established non-EU sellers must register from the first French sale unless using the IOSS/OSS regimes for distance sales; the EU OSS non-EU scheme threshold applies where relevant.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: France is progressively mandating structured electronic invoicing ('facturation électronique') for B2B and B2C transaction reporting: the obligation starts on 1 September 2026 for large enterprises and 1 September 2027 for SMEs/VSEs. Invoices must be transmitted via a certified Plateforme de Dématérialisation Partenaire (PDP) or the public 'Portail Public de Facturation' in EN 16931 syntax, with e-invoice data sent to DGFiP and Customs for e-reporting. There is currently no real-time physical-fiscal stamping regime (unlike the Italian 'stampa fiscale'); clearance is achieved through structured transmission and post-transaction audit.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of tangible goods to destinations outside the EU are exempt with credit for input VAT under CGI Art. 262 I where legal title passes to the non-EU customer and the goods are physically shipped to a non-EU country. Intra-EU supplies are also eligible for zero-rating if the customer supplies a valid VAT ID and the goods are transported to another Member State. Services directly relating to exported goods (e.g., assembly, calibration, logistics) may be zero-rated under CGI Art. 262 II provided the exporter possesses the required evidential documents. The zero-rating must be justified by documentary proof and reflected on the French EC Sales List.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Déclaration en Douane / DAU)
Bill of Lading / Air Waybill / CMR transport document
Inward Remittance Certificate (bank or IRC evidencing receipt of export proceeds)
Commercial invoice with explicit 'TVA non applicable – exportation' or 'exonération de TVA' mention
Packing list and proof of shipment to non-EU destination
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: If a French VAT inspector finds that export proof is missing, false, or the goods are returned to France or another EU Member State, the zero-rating is retroactively reversed: the supplier must pay the 20% VAT and is assessed late-payment interest (0.2% per month). Penalties under CGI Art. 1728 and 1729 range from 40% (deliberate failure to collect/pay VAT) to 80% (fraudulent or abusive 'abus de droit'); customs fraud under the Code des douanes can expose the exporter to a fine of up to three times the value of the goods and, in serious cases, criminal prosecution.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France (BdF), operating within the European System of Central Banks (ESCB) and Governing Council, with monetary sovereignty over the euro delegated to the European Central Bank (ECB). The Board's foreign-account and balance-of-payments statistical regime (NORIF) is administered by the Banque de France as agent of the Direction Générale du Trésor at the Ministère de l'Économie et des Finances; supervision of credit institutions is exercised by the Autorité de Contrôle Prudentiel et de Résolution (ACPR), a twin-peak authority attached to the Banque de France.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The euro is fully convertible, freely floating, and classified as a reserve currency. France operates no exchange-control authorisation system, no administrative convertibility gate, and no legal separation between current-account and capital-account approvals; capital movements are liberalised under Article 63 TFEU and codified in the Code monétaire et financier (Article L.151-1: 'les relations financières avec l'étranger sont libres'). Profit remittance is burdened only by ordinary corporate-law preconditions and tax, not by FX licensing: a French SARL may distribute dividends only out of legally distributable profits verified against the statutory accounts, provided the legal reserve (10% of share capital until it reaches 10% of capital) is funded and net assets remain above share capital. Tax-wise, dividends to an EU/EEA corporate shareholder holding at least 5% for two years attract 0% French withholding under the Parent-Subsidiary Directive (Articles 119 ter and 145 CGI); treaty-reduced rates (typically 5-15%) apply to third-country corporate shareholders, or local 30% flat withholding if no treaty benefit is claimed. The practical constraints are: (i) all cross-border wire transfers must be routed through an ACPR-licensed credit institution under the French intermediation rule; and (ii) the SARL's bank must transmit each cross-border payment to the Banque de France for balance-of-payments statistics; no treasury licence or prior central-bank approval is required for the medical-electronics sector.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory surrender regime exists in France. There is no mandatory timeline for repatriation, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no obligation to credit export proceeds to a designated national account. The SARL may invoice in EUR, USD, or any other currency, hold foreign currency indefinitely in a foreign-currency account with a French authorised intermediary or a foreign bank, and determine freely the commercial moment of conversion. The only legal duties are statistical: (1) credit institutions report cross-border payments with non-residents to the Banque de France as part of balance-of-payments statistics whenever transactions meet the applicable per-transfer itemisation thresholds; (2) where the SARL maintains foreign bank accounts or executes flows outside an authorised intermediary, it must file NORIF (notice of financial relations with the outside world) returns on a monthly/quarterly basis for aggregate annual cross-border flows exceeding the regulatory de minimis, commonly EUR 750,000 as amended, itemising flows above EUR 12,500; and (3) separate customs goods declarations (Intrastat/EX or the common export declaration) continue in parallel. Non-compliance exposes the SARL to administrative fines under Title II of Book III of the Code monétaire et financier, but never blocks convertibility or compels the sale of export receipts.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (compte bloqué) on incorporation; multi-currency operational account (compte courant) in EUR/USD with dedicated trade-finance line
Capital Escrow Account; multi-currency operating account; import/export documentary-LC desk
Blocked capital-deposit account; commercial operating account; SEPA and SWIFT MT103 channels; working-capital and LC facilities

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: BPCE / Banque Populaire & Caisse d'Epargne (Natixis as CIB arm)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Corporate operating account; foreign-exchange forward lines; euro clearing via T2
Corporate operating and escrow accounts; supply-chain finance and guarantee instruments

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility is Low for core treasury and Medium for ancillary euro collections. An EU-passported fintech electronic-money institution (under French law, 'établissement de monnaie électronique', or an EU/EEA EMI passporting into France) may lawfully hold the SARL's e-money, execute SEPA credit transfers, process card receipts, and offer retail-grade FX conversion. It is, however, not a credit institution: it cannot issue or confirm commercial letters of credit, cannot discount or forfait LC documents, cannot grant overdrafts, banker's guarantees, or corporate loans, and generally lacks SWIFT MT103 correspondent relationships and NORIF balance-of-payments reporting infrastructure. For an ISIC 3250 exporter settling through Swift_LC and TT_Wire rails, the EMI can serve only as an auxiliary collection and disbursement channel. A non-EU offshore EMI (e.g., UK, Singapore, or UAE-licensed) has no passport into France and may not provide payment services to French residents, hold the SARL's client funds, or open quasi-IBANs representing French relationships without ACPR registration; using such providers for main trade settlement creates an AML/transborder-banking breach and exposes the gérant to sanctions under Article L.561-4 Code monétaire et financier.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: There is no statutory mandate that directors must appear physically; the AML/CFT due-diligence duty (Articles L.561-5 et seq. Code monétaire et financier) requires the bank to identify the client and beneficial owners before establishing business relations, which can be satisfied by secure video-identification (liveness, document verification, dynamic timestamp) under ACPR guidance. In practice, however, traditional Tier-1 French banks require at least one physical meeting with the gérant and each authorised signatory for a newly incorporated SARL requesting LC and trade lines above EUR 500,000; branch-based remote onboarding is generally denied for first-time corporate clients with non-resident shareholders. Fully remote opening is legally viable and practically available through regulated neo-banks (e.g., Qonto, Shine, Blank), which accept video KYC, but these institutions do not provide documentary credit or substantial working capital. The prudent blueprint: open a Tier-1 account with a physical gérant visit, supplemented by a parallel neo-bank account for daily treasury; keep the same KYC dossier in both channels.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident or multi-layered shareholder structure with no apparent economic substance in France
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Incorporation pack: signed statuts, the RBE beneficial-ownership declaration filed at the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce, Kbis extract issued within last three months, certified corporate group chart with ultimate natural persons, full passport/ID and proof of address for each ultimate beneficial owner, and a written AML/CFT self-assessment memo covering the commercial rationale for the cross-border structure

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unverifiable origin of the capital injection (foreign funds of unknown provenance)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bank statements of each contributing shareholder covering the last 12 months and the routing of the precise funds, signed capital-contribution declaration (apport en numéraire), attestation of the depositary bank or compte-bloqué certificate, tax returns or wealth statements of contributors, and a complete wire-trace (remitter, intermediary, beneficiary) showing no third-party payments

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Missing medical-device regulatory licence at onboarding (sector compliance red flag)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Valid CE certificate issued by a notified body for the multi-parameter ECG monitor, EC Declaration of Conformity, EUDAMED Single Registration Number (SRN), ANSM registration or pre-market filing of the SARL as manufacturer/authorised representative per the French Public Health Code, ISO 13485 certification for the assembly and calibration site, and the summary of technical documentation demonstrating conformity to MDR (EU) 2017/745

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Trade-flow mismatches and opaque invoicing in the medical procurement chain
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed master purchase and distribution contracts, pro-forma and final VAT-compliant invoices, Incoterms clauses (EXW/FCA/CPT), customs export declarations and Intrastat returns, transport documents (B/L, AWB, CMR), delivery confirmations, and a documented transfer-pricing policy for intercompany fees consistent with the French documentation thresholds under Article L.13 AA CGI

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: PEP, sanctions, or embargo exposure of beneficial owners or foreign distributors
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed PEP questionnaire, sanctions screening reports against EU, OFAC, UN, and UK HMT listings for all shareholders, signatories, and material counterparties, export-control assessment (dual-use/EAR classification of the monitor's communication modules), and an attestation of compliance with EU/Russian and other embargo regimes

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Signatories not tax-resident in France, or unclear CRS/FATCA status
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: CRS self-certification forms (Form 101/102) for each controlling person, tax-residency certificates of non-resident shareholders, proof of the SARL's SIREN/SIRET registration, intracommunity VAT number under Article 286 ter CGI, and EORI number, enabling the bank to perform FATCA and CRS reporting at onboarding

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Formative capital: non-resident shareholders subscribe the SARL's share capital by wire-transferring the agreed amount to a French blocked capital-deposit account (compte bloqué) opened in the SARL's name before registration; the bank issues an attestation of the capital deposit, the gérant signs the declaration of no cash in-kind fraud, and the funds are released only after immatriculation at the Greffe. Wire protocol: SWIFT MT103 from the shareholder's own account at an authorised bank, quoting the beneficiary IBAN (FR76-BIC format), the SARL's SIREN/EORI, and the ISO 20022 purpose code 'FIPE' (foreign direct investment in equity) or the bank's internal Banque de France balance-of-payments code for 'apports en capital / souscription d'actions dans une société française'; the remitter name must match the subscriber name exactly — third-party wires are rejected. Treasury injections after formation (shareholder loans or current-account advances): SWIFT MT103 with purpose code 'FIDL' or 'LOAN' backed by a written convention de compte courant d'associé, restated in the annual accounts; inflows exceeding the balance-of-payments de minimis thresholds are reported to the Banque de France either by the receiving credit institution or directly by the SARL under NORIF. A pre-close perimeter check against the French foreign-investment screening decree (Décret n°2023-1293 and Article R.151-3 Code monétaire et financier) must confirm that electronic patient-monitor production is not on the sensitive-activity list; a negative legal memorandum should be retained evidencing that no prior ministerial authorisation is required.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary clear rails: (1) SEPA Credit Transfer (ISO 20022 pain.001) for all euro-denominated payments to EU/EEA suppliers — mandatory for intra-EEA euro flows, settled within one TARGET2 business day with no correspondent charges; (2) SWIFT MT103 via the correspondent network (CHIPS/Fedwire for USD, CHAPS for GBP) for non-euro invoices; (3) Commercial Letters of Credit issued via SWIFT MT700, subject to UCP 600, confirmed where appropriate by a prime bank in the beneficiary country, with settlement via payment against MT754/MT756 and document examination; this is the recommended rail for cross-border procurement of calibrated sensors, PCBs, and display sub-assemblies for the ECG monitor line; (4) Documentary collections (D/P, D/A) and standby LCs (URDG 758 for guarantees) as intermediate instruments for repeat counterparties. All outgoing payments must be matched to underlying contracts, invoices, and customs declarations to withstand bank AML transaction-monitoring; the SARL should maintain an annual rolling trade-finance umbrella limit with its Tier-1 bank, with per-beneficiary KYC updates on any change in the foreign supplier register.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright foreign-exchange forward contracts (achat/vente à terme de devises) on EUR/USD, EUR/GBP, and EUR/CNH with a licensed French credit institution, covered by a treasury policy and board delegation of authority
FX swaps (swaps de change) for short-term rolling of USD/EUR payable and receivable positions, documented under the bank's standard treasury master agreement
Cross-currency interest-rate swaps for long-term financing of the French production facility or equipment imports, permitted subject to EMIR and cleared or margined as applicable

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) against non-convertible or restricted currencies (e.g., CNH or emerging-market currencies as required by distributor invoicing), documented under a 1992/2002 ISDA Master Agreement and subject to EMIR reporting, variation margining, and initial-margin rules if the counterparty group exceeds the applicable average-aggregate-notional threshold

Vanilla FX options (options de change) for sourced-basis hedging of large tender or distribution contracts, subject to MiFID II professional-client suitability assessment and, where applicable, uncleared-margin regulation (UMR) initial-margin obligations

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual approval of accounts and filing of annual accounts
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders and competent Commercial Court Registry (Greffe du tribunal de commerce)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Accounts must generally be approved within six months after the financial year-end and filed within one month after approval, or within two months after approval when filed electronically. A small company may request confidentiality or simplified publication where statutory conditions are satisfied.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing may result in a court injunction, a civil fine generally up to EUR 1,500 (EUR 3,000 for repeat infringement), and judicial enforcement. Persistent inactivity or failure to regularize may lead to administrative or judicial removal from the Commercial Register; no uniform automatic strike-off period applies.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: French corporate income tax return (Form 2065 with annual tax package)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: French Tax Administration (Direction générale des finances publiques)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Generally by the second business day after 1 May for a calendar-year company, or within three months after the financial year-end where the year-end is not 31 December. Electronic filing is mandatory for companies subject to corporate income tax.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing generally attracts a 10% surcharge, potentially increased to 40% or 80% in aggravated cases, plus late-payment interest currently calculated under the applicable statutory rate.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual local business tax compliance for Cotisation Foncière des Entreprises (CFE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: CFE is assessed annually and generally payable electronically by 15 December. A property or activity declaration is required when requested or when establishing, changing, or ceasing an establishment; there is no general annual renewal filing for an unchanged business.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment generally incurs a 5% surcharge and statutory late-payment interest. Failure to provide a required declaration may result in tax reassessment and applicable penalties.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Competent Commercial Court Registry through the French national business register
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: France does not require a routine annual beneficial-owner confirmation. Changes to beneficial ownership or control must generally be filed within 30 days of the relevant change.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file or maintain accurate beneficial-owner information may trigger formal notice, criminal sanctions for responsible persons, and restrictions or enforcement affecting the company's registration status.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A statutory auditor is generally required when the SARL exceeds at least two of three thresholds at the financial year-end: EUR 5 million total balance sheet assets, EUR 10 million net turnover, and 50 average employees. Additional requirements may apply to certain parent, subsidiary, or group structures and where shareholders holding the statutory percentage request an audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French GAAP under the French Accounting Standards Authority (Autorité des normes comptables). IFRS may apply to consolidated accounts where legally permitted or required; IFRS is not generally mandatory for standalone SARL accounts.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: No annual UBO confirmation is required solely because a new year begins. The SARL must review ownership and control information annually as part of its compliance process and file any change generally within 30 days. Share transfers must be documented in writing, recorded in the applicable transfer records, and reflected in the articles or Commercial Register filings where required.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of shareholders and share transfers
Register of shareholders' decisions and meeting minutes
Annual accounts, management reports, and accounting records
Current beneficial-owner information and supporting ownership-control documentation

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: Approximately USD 650-1,950 annually for a commercial registered-office service; France does not generally require a separate resident agent for a French SARL.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Approximately USD 3,000-10,000 annually for a small SARL requiring a statutory auditor; no statutory audit fee applies where the audit threshold is not met and no auditor is otherwise required.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: R&D tax credit (up to 30% of qualifying expenses), accelerated depreciation, targeted tax holidays in overseas territories

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 1201 - Déclaration de résultat, filed electronically via impots.gouv.fr

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross turnover from patient monitor sales and calibration services
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Exclude VAT; report consolidated group revenue
Apply permanent and temporary differences; attach supporting schedules

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: 0.5% of tax due per month of delay, capped at 25%; plus statutory interest at 0.2% per month

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Submit Tax Residency Certificate and DTA relief application to withholding agent with TRC and beneficial ownership declaration
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties 12.8% statutory (reduced to 0-10% under most DTAs); interest 12.8% statutory (reduced to 0-10% under DTAs)

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: French Economic Substance Law requires adequate substance for IP holding, financing, and distribution activities; non-compliance triggers recharacterization and penalties

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate false declaration or understatement of income
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: 80% of evaded tax plus criminal imprisonment of 1 to 5 years
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Personal criminal liability, fines, and disqualification from office

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to maintain contemporaneous TP documentation or aggressive adjustments lacking economic substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: 100% penalty on tax adjustment plus interest and potential 500,000 EUR administrative fine
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Civil restitution obligations and reputational risk

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining French SARL solely for tax residence without real economic activity or substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recharacterization of transactions, denial of deductions, and penalties up to 500,000 EUR
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Imprisonment for fraud, asset seizure, and travel bans
